intro.author: Unknown. The book names no author; a Jewish tradition recorded in the Talmud credited Moses.
intro.written: Uncertain. The story is set in the age of the patriarchs, but scholars' dates for the writing range from Solomon's time to after the exile.
intro.audience: Israel and its wisdom teachers, through a story set outside Israel
intro.setting: Job is a wealthy, devout man from 'the land of Uz,' probably east or southeast of Israel near Edom (Lamentations 4:21). His wealth is counted in herds, and he offers sacrifices himself as head of his family, with no mention of the temple or the Law of Moses. A prose story (chapters 1–2 and 42:7-17) frames a long poem of speeches.
intro.purpose: To wrestle honestly with why the righteous suffer, testing the common belief that God always rewards the good and punishes the wicked in this life.
intro.bigIdea: God is wiser and greater than any formula, and he meets a suffering man who keeps crying out to him.
